name: OpenFileDialog
purpose: An OpenFileDialog shows the standard Windows 'Open' window so the user can choose one or more existing files. Your code receives the selected path.
whenToUse: Let the user pick a file to load, import or attach.
Allow several files by setting Multiselect = true.
Limit choices to certain types with the Filter property.
realWorldExamples: A 'Browse...' button to select an image for a profile.
File > Open in a text editor.
Importing a CSV file into a grid.
defaultAppearance: OpenFileDialog is a non-visual component. When ShowDialog is called, Windows displays its modal Open window with a folder tree, file list, a File name box and a file-type drop-down.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the FileName without checking the dialog result.
commonMistakes.fix: Only use FileName when ShowDialog() returns DialogResult.OK.
Use pairs separated by '|', such as "Text files (*.txt)|*.txt|All files (*.*)|*.*".
Create it in a using block or add it to the form's components so it is released.

relatedNotes.name: SaveFileDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Chooses a file name to write to; it can warn about overwriting.

relatedNotes.name: FolderBrowserDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Chooses a folder instead of a file.

name: SaveFileDialog
purpose: A SaveFileDialog shows the standard Windows 'Save As' window so the user can choose where and under what name to save a file.
whenToUse: Suggest a default name and extension with FileName and DefaultExt.
realWorldExamples: File > Save As in an editor.
Exporting a report to PDF or CSV.
Saving a drawing as a PNG image.
defaultAppearance: SaveFileDialog is a non-visual component. ShowDialog opens the modal Save As window with a folder tree, a File name box and a Save as type list.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the file now exists after the dialog closes.
commonMistakes.fix: The dialog only returns a path; you must write the file yourself.

commonMistakes.mistake: Ignoring the extension the user chose.
commonMistakes.fix: Set AddExtension and DefaultExt, and match the Filter to what you can write.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using FileName if the dialog was cancelled.

relatedNotes.name: OpenFileDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Selects an existing file to read.

relatedNotes.name: FolderBrowserDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Selects a folder, not a file name.

name: FolderBrowserDialog
purpose: A FolderBrowserDialog lets the user choose a folder. The path is returned in SelectedPath.
whenToUse: Pick an output or backup folder.
Choose a root directory to scan for files.
Set a default folder in application settings.
realWorldExamples: Choosing where downloaded files are stored.
Selecting a photo folder to import.
Choosing a project folder in a developer tool.
defaultAppearance: FolderBrowserDialog is a non-visual component. ShowDialog opens a modal window with a folder tree, and a 'Make New Folder' button when ShowNewFolderButton is true.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using SelectedPath when the user cancelled.
commonMistakes.fix: Read SelectedPath only if ShowDialog() returns DialogResult.OK.
Use OpenFileDialog when you need a file; this dialog selects folders only.
Set InitialDirectory or SelectedPath to a sensible starting folder.

relatedNotes.name: OpenFileDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Selects files; it can also be used with a folder to start in.

relatedNotes.name: SaveFileDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Chooses a file name to save to, not just a folder.

name: ColorDialog
purpose: A ColorDialog displays the standard Windows color picker and returns the chosen Color.
whenToUse: Let users customize a background, text or drawing color.
Preview a color before applying it.
realWorldExamples: A 'Choose color' button in a drawing app.
Changing the background color of a note.
Setting a highlight color in settings.
defaultAppearance: ColorDialog is a non-visual component. ShowDialog opens a modal window with a palette of basic colors, custom color slots and, if allowed, a 'Define Custom Colors' area.

commonMistakes.mistake: Applying Color without checking the result.
commonMistakes.fix: Use the color only when ShowDialog() returns DialogResult.OK.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not showing the current color as the starting point.
commonMistakes.fix: Set ColorDialog.Color to the existing color before calling ShowDialog.

commonMistakes.mistake: Losing the user's custom colors between uses.
commonMistakes.fix: Keep the same dialog object, or save and restore the CustomColors array.

relatedNotes.name: FontDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Chooses a font and font color instead of just a color.

relatedNotes.name: OpenFileDialog
relatedNotes.difference: Another standard dialog; it picks files rather than colors.

name: FontDialog
purpose: A FontDialog displays the standard Windows font picker, where the user chooses a font family, style and size, and optionally a color.
whenToUse: Let users change the font of an editor or label.
Choose a font with ShowColor = true to also pick a text color.
Limit choices with MinSize, MaxSize or FixedPitchOnly.
realWorldExamples: Format > Font in a text editor.
Choosing the display font for a report.
A console or code editor font setting.
defaultAppearance: FontDialog is a non-visual component. ShowDialog opens a modal window with lists for Font, Font style and Size, a Sample preview, and optional Effects such as strikeout and underline.

commonMistakes.fix: Apply the Font only when ShowDialog() returns DialogResult.OK.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting that the dialog does not show the current font unless you set it.
commonMistakes.fix: Assign the control's current Font to FontDialog.Font before showing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting the text color to apply by itself.
commonMistakes.fix: Set ShowColor = true and apply the Color property to ForeColor yourself.

relatedNotes.name: RichTextBox
relatedNotes.difference: A common target for the chosen font, using SelectionFont.

relatedNotes.name: TextBox
relatedNotes.difference: Receives the chosen font through its Font property.
